messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] paging @mike @sophia — elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for EU region (svc=prefix-cache). rate ~12% across gateways, spike started ~11:06 UTC. auto-escalation -> paging oncall. :rotating_light:

mike: seeing it, reading graphs now. which shard?

sophia: EU-prefetch pool, shards s-eu-3 / s-eu-4 showing continuous eviction spikes and a bunch of `kv:checksum mismatch` logs.

james: logs snippet from s-eu-3 around spike start:
```
2026-03-15T11:06:12Z ERROR kv/prefix_cache: eviction loop panic: attempted to free key with invalid checksum (key=prefix_0x7f.., shard=s-eu-3)
2026-03-15T11:06:13Z WARN prefetch: scheduling backoff for shard s-eu-3
2026-03-15T11:06:14Z ERROR gateway: 502 upstream timeout (prefix-cache)
```

lina: customer CS reports timeouts for autocomplete and snippet generation in EU. cs-rep posted two logs and customer ids (redacted) in #support.

cs-rep: confirmed ~5 enterprise customers affected, they see repeated 502s and one reports ~30% request failures for a keyflow. They're escalating to their oncall.

mike: immediate mitigation options? can we isolate shard, divert traffic, or enable fallback routing?

sophia: options:
- divert EU requests to fallback prefix-cache read-through to KV store (higher latency, reduces 5xx)
- disable aggressive prefetch on affected shards to stop eviction churn
- run `kv-check --shard s-eu-3 --fix` but that may take minutes and cause IO spike
- tombstone suspected corrupt prefixes then rebuild from origin

james: i'm in favor of divert + disable prefetch as quick wins. i'll open a routing rule to send s-eu-* reads to origin-cache-standby for 10m.

mike: do it. also throttle prefetch and raise eviction_threshold to buy time. can someone create the quick rollback config? @deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: @james requested a dynamic routing change: apply-route --scope=eu --service=prefix-cache --to=origin-cache-standby --ttl=600 --tags=incident-1712349999. queued for approval.

james: approved, applying now.

sophia: disabling prefetch on s-eu-3/s-eu-4: `curl -X POST $SRE_API/shards/s-eu-3/actions/disable_prefetch`

mike: done? status?

sophia: done for both. eviction rate dropped by ~70% in the last 30s, gateways errors dropping to ~6% now.

lina: notifying CS: "we've diverted reads and disabled aggressive prefetch; we expect error rate to continue falling over next 5-10 minutes. investigating root cause and will follow up."

cs-rep: shared update with customers — they appreciate the quick patch but want ETA for full resolution. one customer asked for a postmortem.

james: while diversion is active, i'm running `kv-check --shard s-eu-3 --verify-only` to see scope of corruption. will run --fix after we have metrics.

sophia: observation: a recent config rollback pushed yesterday increased aggressive prefetch window from 20s -> 120s for EU will cause more in-memory entries and faster eviction. suspect config + a small memory leak triggered churn.

mike: can we roll the config back to 20s for EU? risk?

james: low risk, route + prefetch disabled already. i'll rollback config in config-store: `configctl set prefix.prefetch.window 20 --env=eu --reason=\"incident 1712349999 rollback\"`

james: rolled back. monitoring. eviction metrics normalizing, 502s down to ~2% at gateways.

mike: good. next steps: schedule shard-level `kv-check --fix` during quiet window to repair corrupt checksums, and run checksum audit across s-eu cluster. Also create a mitigations runbook entry.

sophia: i'll start a handoff doc in /incident-notes and add steps to disable prefetch, route diversion, and the KV repair playbook. linking here when done.

james: runbook note: avoid running --fix during peak; do staggered fix per shard with `--pause-after=30s` to avoid IO spikes.

lina: CS asked for an estimated RTO. based on current trend, we can say "mitigation in 10-20m, full repair within 4-6 hours". good to confirm?

mike: agree. i'll post external status update.

deploy-bot: routing change completed and verified (deploy-id: r-20260315-1712).

incident-bot: [INCIDENT STATUS] 1712349999 - mitigation active. symptoms: elevated 5xx & gateway timeouts in EU. root cause: prefetch config expansion + eviction churn -> checksum mismatches on s-eu shards (investigating). impact: partial customer latency and timeouts. workaround: route-to-origin + disable-prefetch applied. oncall: @mike -> handing to @sophia for longer-term repair at 11:45 UTC.

sophia: taking handoff. final checklist:
- schedule kv-check --fix for s-eu-3 and s-eu-4 at 15:30 UTC, staggered
- run checksum audit script across EU shards: `./tools/checksum_audit --region eu --out=checksums-eu-1712349999.csv`
- add regression alert for prefetch.window config changes

ryan: product note: flagging this for postmortem; need customer-impact timeline and affected request paths. will join the post-incident review.

mike: handing off pager to @sophia at 11:45 UTC. i'll stay available for questions.

sophia: acknowledged. closing temporary routing in 10m if stable; will update when repair complete.

cs-rep: customers updated. one asked for a short postmortem and timeline.

mike: great work team. follow-up: include exact config diff in postmortem and correlate with deploy history.

sophia: marking incident as INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED (partial) for now. will reopen if errors spike after fixes.

incident-bot: [CLOSED] 1712349999 - mitigation applied, error rates reduced to baseline. follow-up tasks assigned in /incident-notes/1712349999 (owners: sophia, james, lina).
